text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Mines Minister Christon Tembo says government has taken measures to ensure that there is no asset stripping in Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines (ZCCM) before it is privatised.
- The Committee for Clean Campaign, which oversaw last year's general elections, demands that the police return documents they confisticated in November.
- The central bank says the closed African Commercial Bank can reopen if management sources funding.
- Minister without portfolio Michael Sata warns non-governmental organisations to stay away from politics or face the government's wrath.
- The Committee for a Clean Campaign, an election watchdog group, says the judiciary has lost its credibility by being partisan to the ruling party.
- Zimbabwe increases tariffs on cement imports from Zambia from 0.15 Zimbabwe dollars to 130 dollars per tonne.
